advances: The comparable two-center label budgets transfer to the entire original affine law, allowing arbitrary outside singleton atoms and arbitrary mixtures with unrestricted zero-center and one-center factors. Disjoint two-center cores require no comparison of means. A single label selection across each whole conditional product, followed by one capacity transfer across all leaves, pays one dimension-independent coefficient. This closes the outside-mass transfer for the comparable overlapping-core branch; it does not settle disparate overlapping means, more than two centers, or the locked mixed-integer target.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. All predecessors used are the five declared accepted facts, with their exact roles and normalization maps specified above.
proof:
First note that \(\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\subseteq Q_i\) and hence \(A_i=\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\cap\mathbb Z^{n_i}\). Thus the completeness hypothesis of accepted fact 9e1805a461c7be2c applies to each two-center support.

We first verify the geometry and construct partitions with exact additive capacities. If \(\mathcal C_i\) is empty, distinct atoms have distinct coordinatewise parity: otherwise their midpoint would be an integral point of \(Q_i\), and therefore a member of \(\mathcal C_i\). Partition \(A_i\) into its singleton atoms. Give every piece capacity one; the sum of its capacities is exactly \(K_i=|A_i|\).

If \(\mathcal C_i=\lbrace c_i\rbrace\), the core \(R_i=A_i\cap(2c_i-A_i)\) is nonempty and is a complete convex lattice support symmetric about \(c_i\). Accepted fact 60336390757d4ce6 proves that its only nontrivial midpoint center is \(c_i\), it occupies exactly \(M_i=(|R_i|+1)/2\) parity classes, and every outside atom occupies a singleton class disjoint from those classes. Partition \(A_i\) into \(R_i\) and the singleton outside atoms. Give the core capacity \(M_i\) and each singleton capacity one. The sum of the capacities is exactly \(K_i=M_i+|A_i\setminus R_i|\).

Now suppose there are exactly two centers. By accepted fact 9e1805a461c7be2c, every parity class contains at most two atoms, the centers have different parity, and each full core \(R_{i,a}\) is a complete symmetric support with exactly the one nontrivial midpoint center \(c_{i,a}\). That fact gives the exact identities
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{i,0}\cap R_{i,1}
&=\lbrace c_{i,a}:c_{i,a}\in R_{i,1-a},\ a\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace\rbrace,\\
\bigl|\lbrace x+2\mathbb Z^{n_i}:x\in U_i\rbrace\bigr|
&=M_{i,0}+M_{i,1}-q_{\mathrm{ov},i},\\
K_i&=M_{i,0}+M_{i,1}-q_{\mathrm{ov},i}+s_i.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$
The atoms outside \(U_i\) have distinct singleton parity classes disjoint from all classes of \(U_i\). If \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}=0\), the cores are disjoint in both atoms and parity classes. Partition into those two complete one-center cores and the individual outside atoms. Assign capacities \(M_{i,0},M_{i,1}\), and one respectively. Their sum is exactly \(K_i\).

The disjoint case is possible. In dimension two, \(A=\lbrace0,1\rbrace\times\lbrace-1,0,1\rbrace\) is the complete lattice census of \([0,1]\times[-1,1]\). An integral midpoint of distinct atoms must have equal first coordinates, because the average of zero and one is not integral. In a fixed first-coordinate fiber, the only distinct second coordinates with integral average are -1 and 1. Thus its centers are exactly \((0,0),(1,0)\), and their full cores are the two disjoint three-point fibers. They have disjoint parity classes and total capacity \(2+2=4\).

If \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\in\lbrace1,2\rbrace\), partition \(A_i\) into the single union piece \(U_i\) and the individual outside atoms. Give \(U_i\) capacity \(k_{i,U_i}=M_{i,0}+M_{i,1}-q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\) and every outside singleton capacity one. Again (5) makes the total capacity exactly \(K_i\).

This union need not be complete, and no completeness assertion for it will be used. It is closed under integral midpoints of its atoms: the midpoint of any distinct same-parity atoms of \(U_i\) is a member of \(\mathcal C_i\), so it is one of the two centers, both of which belong to \(U_i\). Each center remains a nontrivial midpoint center because its full core remains present. Its full reflected row inside \(U_i\) is exactly \(R_{i,a}\), since
\(R_{i,a}\subseteq U_i\cap(2c_{i,a}-U_i)\subseteq A_i\cap(2c_{i,a}-A_i)=R_{i,a}\).
Every other supported center has a singleton reflected row. All parity classes still contain at most two points, and the centers retain their different parities. Consequently \(U_i\), equipped with its exact conditional law from (2), satisfies every geometric hypothesis of the exact two-hub table in accepted fact a87effc3cf58f392. In that table the label-a pair count is exactly \(m_{i,a}=M_{i,a}-1\), its row cardinality is \(h_{i,a}=2m_{i,a}+1=|R_{i,a}|\), its overlap is \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\), and its occupied count is
\(K=k_{i,U_i}=m_{i,0}+m_{i,1}+2-q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\).

Write \(\mathcal D_i\) for the partition just constructed, and \(k_{i,D}\) for a piece's assigned positive integer capacity. In every case
\(\sum_{D\in\mathcal D_i}k_{i,D}=K_i\le2^{n_i}\).
For every piece define
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_{i,D}&=\sum_{x\in D}e^{\ell_i\cdot x},&
\beta_{i,D}&=\sum_{x\in D}p_{i,x}=\frac{Z_{i,D}}{Z_i},\\
\pi_{i,D}(x)&=\frac{p_{i,x}}{\beta_{i,D}}
             =\frac{e^{\ell_i\cdot x}}{Z_{i,D}}\quad(x\in D).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$
These conditional laws are used only for the leaf calculations below. The original law remains \(p_{i,x}=e^{\ell_i\cdot x}/Z_i\). All pieces are nonempty, so every mass \(\beta_{i,D}\) is positive.

We prove one common moment bound for an arbitrary leaf of this partition. Fix \(\lambda=(D_1,\ldots,D_L)\in\prod_i\mathcal D_i\), and put
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_\lambda&=\prod_iD_i,&
\alpha_\lambda&=\prod_i\beta_{i,D_i},&
k_\lambda&=\prod_ik_{i,D_i},\\
P_\lambda(X)&=\prod_i\pi_{i,D_i}(x_i)
 =\frac{\prod_ie^{\ell_i\cdot x_i}}{\prod_iZ_{i,D_i}}
 =\frac{P_X}{\alpha_\lambda}\quad(X\in A_\lambda).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$
For this fixed leaf abbreviate \(\pi_i=\pi_{i,D_i}\) and \(k_i=k_{i,D_i}\). These are exact aliases confined to the leaf proof; they do not redefine the original \(p_i,P,Z_i,K_i\). Each block is either a singleton, a complete one-center symmetric core, or an overlapping two-core union. We will show \(M_2(P_\lambda)\ge c k_\lambda^{-2}\) with the same c for every possible mixed leaf.

For a supported center j in a leaf block, use the canonical reflected row
\(R_{i,j}^{\lambda}=D_i\cap(2j-D_i)\), and the quantities \(H_{\pi_i},b(\pi_i),\kappa_{i,j},Y_{i,j},V_{i,j},q_{i,j}\) of accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705, with its law \(p_i\) replaced by the leaf law \(\pi_i\) and its support \(A_i\) replaced by \(D_i\). In particular \(Y_{i,j}(x)=\tfrac12\log(\pi_i(x)/\pi_i(2j-x))\), and \(H\) counts each nonzero orientation and the central atom once. Put \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}=k_i^2\sum_{x\in D_i}\pi_i(x)^3\). A leaf block is active precisely when \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}<1\). For an inactive block select singleton auxiliary rows at every center; then its selected scaled energy is \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda}\ge1\), and its selected price is zero. Singleton blocks are always inactive.

For an active one-center core, translate its center c to zero for the scalar calculation. Its translated law is exactly
\(e^{\ell_i\cdot u}/\overline Z_i\), with \(\overline Z_i=e^{-\ell_i\cdot c}Z_{i,D_i}\); translation bijects ambient containing halfspaces and does not alter reflected energies or scores. Let B consist of zero and one representative of each nonzero antipodal pair after translation. Then \(|B|=k_i\). Accepted fact 60336390757d4ce6, using the pair-count normalization proved there, gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_i&=\frac1{k_i}\sum_{b\in B}\cosh(\ell_i\cdot b),&
t_i&=\log(2\mu_i),\\
d_i&=-\log A_{0,i}^{\lambda},&
g_i&=\log(k_i^2b(\pi_i))>0,\\
d_i&\le2^{40}e^{-t_i}g_i,&
\nu_i:=\sum_jq_{i,j}V_{i,j}&\le2^{40}t_i^2g_i.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$
Here the scalar M of 60336390757d4ce6 equals this block's \(k_i\); its \(\widetilde A_0,\widetilde d,\widetilde g\) are exactly \(A_{0,i}^{\lambda},d_i,g_i\). Its unhatted reflected quantities have the canonical meaning just specified. No substitution of occupied counts into an ambient-normalized activity condition is being made. The earlier accepted fact 1b91f86ed4c91107 supplies the one-center multiscale mechanism, while (8) uses the occupied-count strengthening established in 60336390757d4ce6.

Regard such a block as having one label, corresponding to its unique nontrivial center. Give it \(\gamma_i=g_i\), \(\delta_i=d_i\), and parameter \(t_i\). For the empty label selection its logarithmic scaled energy is exactly \(-\delta_i\), and its price is zero. For the full selection its logarithmic scaled energy is exactly \(\gamma_i\), and its price is \(\nu_i\). Because \(C=2\cdot2^{80}+4\ge2^{40}\), (8) gives the common budgets \(\delta_i\le Ce^{-t_i}\gamma_i\) and \(\nu_i\le Ct_i^2\gamma_i\).

For an active overlapping two-center block, use the table budgets of accepted fact a87effc3cf58f392 with the following exact map. Its atom set X is \(D_i=U_i\), its original table law p is our exact conditional \(\pi_i\), and its original table normalizer Z is \(Z_{i,U_i}\) with weights \(w_{i,x}=e^{\ell_i\cdot x}\). Its \(K,m_a,h_a,a_a,S_a\) are \(k_i,m_{i,a},|R_{i,a}|,a_{i,a},S_{i,a}\) respectively. In particular all its table masses are divided by \(Z_{i,U_i}\), with no further normalization. Every label-a pair \(c_{i,a}\pm v_{i,a,r}\) has probabilities \(a_{i,a}e^{u_{i,a,r}},a_{i,a}e^{-u_{i,a,r}}\), where \(u_{i,a,r}=\ell_i\cdot v_{i,a,r}\). Thus its mean and parameter are
\(\mu_{i,a}=M_{i,a}^{-1}(1+\sum_{r=1}^{m_{i,a}}\cosh u_{i,a,r})\) and \(t_{i,a}=\log(2\mu_{i,a})\), exactly the means in (2).

The factor \(\beta_{i,U_i}\) cancels from \(S_{i,a}/a_{i,a}\), proving the asserted invariance of the means. It does not cancel from the cubic sum: the exact activity relation is (2). Since this leaf block is active, the conditional comparison assumed in (2) applies. Hence a87effc3cf58f392 provides nonnegative \(\gamma_{i,a},\delta_{i,a}\), simultaneously for every subset \(\mathcal S\subseteq\lbrace0,1\rbrace\), such that
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{i,\mathcal S}^{\lambda}
&=A_{0,i}^{\lambda}+
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal S}4m_{i,a}(m_{i,a}+1)k_i^2a_{i,a}^{3},\\
\log A_{i,\mathcal S}^{\lambda}
&\ge\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}\gamma_{i,a}
     -\sum_{a\notin\mathcal S}\delta_{i,a},\\
\delta_{i,a}&\le Ce^{-t_{i,a}}\gamma_{i,a},&
\widehat\nu_{i,\mathcal S}&\le C\sum_{a\in\mathcal S}t_{i,a}^{2}\gamma_{i,a}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
$$
The selected rows are the full row \(R_{i,a}\) at each selected center and the singleton row at every other supported center. Since exact midpoint equality makes each full row's geometric law uniform, its selected scaled energy is exactly \(k_i^2\widehat b_i=A_{i,\mathcal S}^{\lambda}\), and its selected price is the \(\widehat\nu_{i,\mathcal S}\) in (9). Inactive overlapping unions use only singleton rows and require no comparison. The one-label and two-label budgets therefore have exactly the same form, with the same C.

We now perform one binning over all labels of all active blocks in this mixed leaf. For integers \(m\ge0\), let \(I_m\) consist of the active labels whose parameter t lies in \([m,m+1)\), and put \(G_m=\sum_{e\in I_m}\gamma_e\), where e denotes either a one-center label or one of the two-center labels. All parameters satisfy \(t\ge\log2\), and only finitely many bins are nonempty. Retain all labels of a bin if and only if \(G_m\ge4C(m+1)^2\). Each block uses the selected rows determined by its retained labels.

For a retained bin set \(W_m=C(m+1)^2G_m\). Its labels contribute at most \(W_m\) to the total selected price, and \(G_m\ge2\sqrt{W_m}\). For a discarded bin the lost logarithmic energy is at most
\(\sum_{e\in I_m}\delta_e\le Ce^{-m}G_m<4C^2e^{-m}(m+1)^2\), with zero loss for an empty bin. Since
\(\sum_{m\ge0}(m+1)^2r^m=(1+r)/(1-r)^3\) and \(e^{-1}<1/2\), all discarded deficits sum to at most \(D=48C^2\). Summing the one-label energy equalities and the two-label inequalities (9), and including the nonnegative inactive energies, gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
S_g:=\sum_i\log(k_i^2\widehat b_i)
&\ge\sum_{m\text{ retained}}G_m-D\\
&\ge2\sum_{m\text{ retained}}\sqrt{W_m}-D
 \ge2\sqrt{\sum_i\widehat\nu_i}-D.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
$$
Here \(\widehat\nu_i\) is the selected price of block i. Indeed (8)-(9) give \(\sum_i\widehat\nu_i\le\sum_{m\text{ retained}}W_m\), and the sum of nonnegative square roots is at least the square root of their sum. This includes no active blocks or no retained bins.

For completeness, verify the selected source for the actual conditional product \(P_\lambda\) without paying a separate coefficient for either block type. Denote the chosen symmetric row at j by \(\widehat R_{i,j}\), and define
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat H_i(j)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat R_{i,j}}
 \sqrt{\pi_i(x)\pi_i(2j-x)},&
\widehat b_i&=\sum_j\pi_i(j)\widehat H_i(j)^2,\\
\widehat\kappa_{i,j}(x)&=\frac{\sqrt{\pi_i(x)\pi_i(2j-x)}}{\widehat H_i(j)},&
\widehat q_{i,j}&=\frac{\pi_i(j)\widehat H_i(j)^2}{\widehat b_i},\\
\widehat V_{i,j}&=\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_{i,j}}Y_{i,j}^2,&
\widehat\nu_i&=\sum_j\widehat q_{i,j}\widehat V_{i,j}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
$$
These are the canonical selected-row quantities used by accepted facts 1b91f86ed4c91107, 60336390757d4ce6, and a87effc3cf58f392, with the leaf law \(\pi_i\). They preserve the normalizer \(Z_{i,D_i}\) in (6). Reflection preserves each auxiliary row law and reverses its score, giving zero score mean, including singleton rows.

For a supported \(J=(j_i)\), put \(\widehat R_J=\prod_i\widehat R_{i,j_i}\), \(\widehat H_\lambda(J)=\prod_i\widehat H_i(j_i)\), \(\widehat\kappa_J=\bigotimes_i\widehat\kappa_{i,j_i}\), \(Y_J(X)=\sum_iY_{i,j_i}(x_i)\), and \(\sigma_J^2=\sum_i\widehat V_{i,j_i}\). Independence and direct substitution give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}Y_J&=0,&
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}Y_J^2&=\sigma_J^2,\\
P_\lambda(X)&=\widehat H_\lambda(J)\widehat\kappa_J(X)e^{Y_J(X)}
\quad(X\in\widehat R_J).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
$$
The probability in (12) is exactly that in (7), with every conditional normalizer intact. Any ambient closed halfspace containing J contains at least one endpoint of each distinct reflected pair \(X,2J-X\), as well as J itself. The reflection-orbit argument of accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705 therefore gives, directly for the selected rows,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{P_\lambda}(J)
&\ge\frac12\sum_{X\in\widehat R_J}
       \min\lbrace P_\lambda(X),P_\lambda(2J-X)\rbrace\\
&=\frac{\widehat H_\lambda(J)}2
   \mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}e^{-|Y_J|}
 \ge\frac{\widehat H_\lambda(J)}2e^{-\sigma_J}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
$$
The oriented sum counts each noncentral orbit twice before the factor one half and uses only half of the central mass. The last inequality is Jensen followed by Cauchy--Schwarz. These statements hold for every containing halfspace in \(\mathbb R^N\), regardless of the affine rank of the leaf support.

Let \(\widehat q=\bigotimes_i\widehat q_i\). The exact identities
\(P_\lambda(J)\widehat H_\lambda(J)^2=(\prod_i\widehat b_i)\prod_i\widehat q_{i,j_i}\) and
\(\mathbb E_{\widehat q}\sigma_J^2=\sum_i\widehat\nu_i\)
show, on squaring (13) and averaging under the entire \(P_\lambda\), that
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P_\lambda)
&\ge\frac14\left(\prod_i\widehat b_i\right)
       \mathbb E_{\widehat q}e^{-2\sigma_J}\\
&\ge\frac14\left(\prod_i\widehat b_i\right)
       \exp\left(-2\sqrt{\sum_i\widehat\nu_i}\right)
 \ge\frac{e^{-D}}{4k_\lambda^2}=c k_\lambda^{-2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
$$
The middle inequality again uses Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz, and the last is (10). Thus one and the same coefficient works for every heterogeneous leaf. In particular no per-factor or separate one-center and two-center coefficients have been multiplied.

Return to the entire original P. The leaves partition \(\prod_iA_i\), their positive masses satisfy \(\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda=1\), and their capacities satisfy the exact identity
\(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda=\prod_i\sum_{D\in\mathcal D_i}k_{i,D}=\prod_iK_i=\mathcal K\).
For J in leaf \(A_\lambda\) and every ambient closed halfspace \(\mathcal H\) containing J, one has \(P(\mathcal H)\ge\alpha_\lambda P_\lambda(\mathcal H)\). Taking the infimum over the same ambient halfspaces yields \(\tau_P(J)\ge\alpha_\lambda\tau_{P_\lambda}(J)\). Hence (14) and Holder's inequality imply
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P)
&\ge\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda^3M_2(P_\lambda)
 \ge c\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda^3}{k_\lambda^2}
 \ge c\left(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\right)^{-2}
 =c\mathcal K^{-2},\\
1=\sum_\lambda\alpha_\lambda
&=\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda}{k_\lambda^{2/3}}k_\lambda^{2/3}
 \le\left(\sum_\lambda\frac{\alpha_\lambda^3}{k_\lambda^2}\right)^{1/3}
      \left(\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\right)^{2/3}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$
This is the exact original-law capacity transfer of accepted fact 60336390757d4ce6, now supplied with the common mixed-leaf bound (14). The original normalizer \(\prod_iZ_i\) remains the one in (1) throughout this averaging. Since \(K_i\le2^{n_i}\), one has \(\mathcal K\le2^N\). Finally Jensen under the entire original P gives
\(M_3(P)=\mathbb E_P(\tau_P^2)^{3/2}\ge M_2(P)^{3/2}\), proving (4).

The convex hull of a finite Cartesian product is the product of its factor convex hulls: multiply the finite convex-combination coefficients to obtain the nontrivial inclusion. Intersecting with \(\mathbb Z^N\), using completeness in each factor, proves the final complete product census. No part of the proof needs full affine dimension, a positive selected variance, or convex completeness of an overlapping union.
statement:
Let \(L\ge1\) and \(n_1,\ldots,n_L\ge1\) be integers. For every i, let \(Q_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be convex, let \(A_i=Q_i\cap\mathbb Z^{n_i}\) be finite and nonempty, and assume that
\(\mathcal C_i=\lbrace(x+y)/2:x,y\in A_i,\ x\ne y,\ (x+y)/2\in\mathbb Z^{n_i}\rbrace\)
has cardinality at most two. For arbitrary \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), retain the entire original affine laws and normalizers
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{i,x}&=e^{\ell_i\cdot x},& Z_i&=\sum_{x\in A_i}w_{i,x},
&p_{i,x}&=\frac{w_{i,x}}{Z_i},\\
P&=\bigotimes_{i=1}^Lp_i,& N&=\sum_{i=1}^Ln_i,
&K_i&=\bigl|\lbrace x+2\mathbb Z^{n_i}:x\in A_i\rbrace\bigr|,
\qquad \mathcal K=\prod_iK_i.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$
Every law is extended by zero off its support.

For each i with exactly two centers, enumerate them as \(c_{i,0},c_{i,1}\), and define the full reflected cores and their canonical capacities by
\(R_{i,a}=A_i\cap(2c_{i,a}-A_i)\),
\(M_{i,a}=(|R_{i,a}|+1)/2\), and \(m_{i,a}=M_{i,a}-1\), for \(a\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace\).
Let \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}=|R_{i,0}\cap R_{i,1}|\), \(U_i=R_{i,0}\cup R_{i,1}\), and \(s_i=|A_i\setminus U_i|\).
The geometric assertions of accepted fact 9e1805a461c7be2c imply that \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\in\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace\), \(m_{i,a}\ge1\), and that the occupied parity count of \(U_i\) is
\(k_{i,U_i}=M_{i,0}+M_{i,1}-q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\), with \(K_i=k_{i,U_i}+s_i\).
Here \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\) is the overlap called t in that predecessor; it is unrelated to the auxiliary center probabilities used below.

Only when \(q_{\mathrm{ov},i}\in\lbrace1,2\rbrace\), impose the following conditional hypothesis. Define the exact conditional union law, mass, and normalizer by
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_{i,U_i}&=\sum_{x\in U_i}w_{i,x},&
\beta_{i,U_i}&=\frac{Z_{i,U_i}}{Z_i},&
\pi_{i,U_i}(x)&=\frac{p_{i,x}}{\beta_{i,U_i}}
              =\frac{w_{i,x}}{Z_{i,U_i}}\quad(x\in U_i),\\
a_{i,a}&=\pi_{i,U_i}(c_{i,a}),&
S_{i,a}&=\sum_{x\in R_{i,a}\setminus\lbrace c_{i,a}\rbrace}\pi_{i,U_i}(x),&
\mu_{i,a}&=\frac{S_{i,a}/a_{i,a}+2}{2M_{i,a}},\\
A_{0,i,U_i}&=k_{i,U_i}^{\,2}\sum_{x\in U_i}\pi_{i,U_i}(x)^3
 =\frac{k_{i,U_i}^{\,2}}{\beta_{i,U_i}^{\,3}}
   \sum_{x\in U_i}p_{i,x}^3.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$
Require \(\max(\mu_{i,0},\mu_{i,1})\le2\min(\mu_{i,0},\mu_{i,1})\) whenever \(A_{0,i,U_i}<1\). Inactive conditional unions, for which \(A_{0,i,U_i}\ge1\), are unrestricted. There is no mean condition on zero-center or one-center factors, or on two-center factors with disjoint cores. The means in (2) are unchanged if both their numerator masses and hub probabilities are computed using the original \(p_i\). The activity test in (2) is specifically the conditional test with capacity \(k_{i,U_i}\).

Use precisely the actual depth and moment conventions of accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_P(J)&=\inf\lbrace P(\mathcal H):\mathcal H\subseteq\mathbb R^N
 \text{ is a closed halfspace containing }J\rbrace,\\
M_2(P)&=\sum_JP_J\tau_P(J)^2,&
M_3(P)&=\sum_JP_J\tau_P(J)^3.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$
With the absolute constants \(C=2\cdot2^{80}+4\) and \(c=\tfrac14\exp(-48C^2)>0\), one has
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P)&\ge c\mathcal K^{-2}\ge c4^{-N},\\
M_3(P)&\ge c^{3/2}\mathcal K^{-3}\ge c^{3/2}8^{-N}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$
The product support is its complete convex lattice census. Lower-dimensional supports, singleton factors, zero score variances, and arbitrary positive or zero overlap counts are included. Every depth in the proof is measured with ambient halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^N\).
